existing_roles.title: Director, Quality
existing_roles.description:
Our mission at ŌURA is to empower every person to own their inner potential. Our award-winning products help our global community gain a deeper knowledge of their readiness, activity, and sleep quality by using their Oura Ring and its connected app. We've helped millions of people understand and improve their health by providing daily insights and practical steps to inspire healthy lifestyles.

Empowering the world starts with living our values and empowering our team. As a quickly growing company focused on helping people live healthier and happier lives, we ensure that our team members have what they need to do their best work — both in and out of the office.

We’re looking for a Director, Quality to lead quality strategy and execution across Oura’s global engineering organization and supply chain.

### **What You Will Do:**

* In this role, you will ensure that quality and reliability are designed into our products, components, suppliers, and manufacturing processes from concept through development, launch, ramp, and sustaining operations. You will lead a global team of quality professionals and partner closely with Product Development, Hardware, Software, Reliability, Manufacturing, Supply Chain, Customer Experience, and external suppliers.
* You will connect customer and field needs to engineering requirements, component controls, supplier capability, manufacturing performance, and product reliability. Your team will help Oura identify risks early, make evidence-based decisions, prevent defects, and resolve complex issues with durable corrective actions.
* This is a broad, highly cross-functional leadership role for an experienced quality executive who can set strategy, develop talent, influence engineering and operations leaders, and engage deeply in both product and supply chain quality when needed.
* Set the quality strategy: Define Oura’s quality vision, operating model, standards, metrics, and priorities across product development, components, suppliers, manufacturing, reliability, and the field.
* Lead and develop a global quality organization: Build, mentor, and manage a high-performing team across product quality, component quality, supplier quality, manufacturing quality, reliability, program quality, and sustaining quality.
* Embed quality across the product lifecycle: Establish effective quality gates and decision criteria from concept and architecture through EVT, DVT, PVT, launch, ramp, and sustaining.
* Partner with engineering and product leaders: Influence product architecture, design decisions, materials, specifications, interfaces, validation plans, and manufacturability to prevent quality and reliability issues.
* Strengthen component and supplier quality: Translate product requirements into component specifications, supplier quality requirements, qualification plans, control plans, inspection strategies, and process controls. Drive supplier capability and performance across the global supply chain.
* Drive manufacturing readiness and performance: Ensure production processes are validated and controlled, with appropriate PFMEA, process capability, measurement systems, yield targets, traceability, reaction plans, and continuous improvement mechanisms.
* Lead risk-based quality planning: Establish disciplined use of DFMEA, PFMEA, reliability planning, design reviews, tolerance analysis, GR&R, SPC, DOE, and risk-based verification and validation.
* Own complex problem solving: Lead containment, failure analysis, root-cause investigation, corrective action, preventive action, and verification of effectiveness for product, component, supplier, manufacturing, reliability, and field issues.
* Build strong field-quality feedback loops: Use warranty, returns, customer support, field failure, reliability, manufacturing, and supplier data to identify systemic risks and drive improvements that reduce member impact and cost of poor quality.
* Lead launch and ramp readiness: Review product and component qualification, supplier capability, manufacturing readiness, validation evidence, yield, open risks, reliability results, and corrective actions before launch and ramp decisions.
* Govern quality-related changes: Ensure design, material, component, supplier, process, software, and manufacturing changes are evaluated for quality and reliability impact and implemented consistently through ECR/ECN and change-control processes.
* Establish a data-driven quality operating system: Define leading and lagging indicators across development, suppliers, manufacturing, and the field. Improve data quality, traceability, dashboards, and escalation mechanisms.
* Drive continuous improvement: Reduce defects, escapes, returns, warranty claims, rework, scrap, and other sources of cost of poor quality while improving product reliability, supplier performance, and customer experience.
* Influence cross-functional decisions: Provide clear, risk-based recommendations when quality, schedule, cost, performance, capacity, and supply continuity priorities compete.
* Communicate with senior leadership: Present concise assessments of product risk, supplier and manufacturing performance, launch readiness, field quality, and improvement priorities.
* Build a culture of prevention and accountability: Make quality a shared responsibility across engineering and operations, with clear ownership for requirements, validation, supplier controls, manufacturing execution, and sustained performance.

This is a hybrid role out of our San Francisco office.

### **What you'll bring**

* 15+ years of experience in product quality, supplier quality, manufacturing quality, reliability, operations quality, or a related engineering discipline, including significant people leadership experience.
* Demonstrated success leading quality for complex, high-volume consumer electronics, wearable, medical-adjacent, or similarly reliability-sensitive products.
* Experience leading and developing teams across one or more of the following areas: product quality, component quality, supplier quality, manufacturing quality, reliability, program quality, or sustaining quality.
* A track record of establishing quality strategy, operating mechanisms, and measurable improvements from early product development through launch and sustaining.
* Strong understanding of product development, design verification and validation, component qualification, reliability engineering, supplier quality, manufacturing processes, and production ramp.
* Strong command of quality and problem-solving methods, including FMEA, 8D, CAPA, SPC, GR&R, DOE, root-cause analysis, control plans, and process capability.
* Experience using engineering, field, warranty, customer support, supplier, and manufacturing data to identify systemic risks and drive corrective action.
* Demonstrated ability to influence engineering, operations, suppliers, and executive leadership without relying solely on direct authority.
* Experience with engineering change control, supplier changes, component qualification, process validation, manufacturing readiness, or production quality improvement.
* Strong understanding of DFM/DFA, GD&T, Lean and Six Sigma principles, measurement systems, and quality management systems.
* Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to translate complex technical risks into concise decisions and actions.
* A self-directed, pragmatic, and resilient leadership style, with a willingness to engage deeply in details while maintaining a strategic perspective.
* Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical, Electrical, Industrial, Systems, Manufacturing, or a related engineering field required; advanced degree or quality certification is a plus.
* Preferred qualifications
* Experience with both product quality and supplier or manufacturing quality, or demonstrated ability to operate effectively across both domains.
* Experience with batteries, electronics, sensors, RF systems, precision mechanics, adhesives, miniaturized assemblies, or other demanding product technologies.
* Experience leading quality for products that combine hardware, firmware, software, and cloud-enabled member experiences.
* Experience building or scaling quality management systems during rapid company growth.
* Familiarity with product safety, regulatory, compliance, traceability, and risk-management requirements relevant to wearable technology.
* Experience with supplier development, APQP, PPAP, SCAR processes, multi-source strategies, capacity expansion, or major manufacturing transitions.
* Experience working across multiple countries, engineering sites, suppliers, and manufacturing partners.

### **Nice to have:**

* HW Experience
* Global distributor teams
* grown and org

### **Benefits**

At Ōura, we care about you and your well-being. Everyone here at Ōura has a ring of their own and we are continually looking to improve employee health.

What we offer:

* Competitive salary and equity packages
* Health, dental, vision insurance, and mental health resources
* An Ōura Ring of your own plus employee discounts for friends & family
* 20 days of paid time off plus 13 paid holidays plus 8 days of flexible wellness time off
* Paid sick leave and parental leave

Ōura takes a market-based approach to pay, which may vary depending on your location. US locations are categorized into tiers based on a cost of labor index for that geographic area. While most offers will be closer to the starting range, successful candidates' pay will be determined based on job-related skills, experience, qualifications, work location, internal peer equity, and market conditions. These ranges may be modified in the future.

Region 1 $226,000-$266,000
 
Region 2 $MIN- $MID
 
Region 3 $MIN- $MID

A recruiter can determine your Region based on your US location.

We are not considering candidates residing in the following states: Alaska (AK), Delaware (DE), Iowa (IA), Mississippi (MS), Nebraska (NE), South Dakota (SD), West Virginia (WV), and Wisconsin (WI).

ŌURA is proud to be an equal opportunity workplace. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees. Individuals seeking employment at ŌURA are considered without regard to age, ancestry, color, gender (including pregnancy, childbirth, or related medical conditions), gender identity or expression, genetic information, marital status, medical condition, mental or physical disability, national origin, protected family care or medical leave status, race, religion (including beliefs and practices or the absence thereof), sexual orientation, military or veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state, or local laws. We will not tolerate discrimination or harassment based on any of these characteristics.

We will work to ensure individuals with disabilities are provided reasonable accommodation to participate in the interview process, to perform essential job functions, and to receive other benefits and privileges of employment.

We’ve been alerted to scammers posing as ŌURA recruiters, especially for remote roles. Please note:

Stay cautious and protect your personal details.

existing_roles.title: Head of Manufacturing Engineering (US)
existing_roles.description:
**About Genesis**
=================

We are a full-stack general-purpose robot company, born across San Francisco and Paris and bound by a single mission: to make general-purpose robots a reality, unlocking infinite physical labor for the world and freeing people for creativity, exploration, and the pursuits they love for their own sake.

We are French and American by birth and global by nature. We are backed by partners who share our vision, including Eclipse, Khosla Ventures, Bpifrance, and HSG, alongside Eric Schmidt, Xavier Niel, Daniela Rus, and Vladlen Koltun. Our people work across the Bay Area and Europe, building the engine that will teach robots to do real work in the real world. We recently unveiled Eno, our wheeled, dexterous robot powered by our GENE foundation model, and we are starting to put it to work with real customers.

**The role**
------------

We build general-purpose robots, and next year we start building them in volume. You will be the manufacturing leader who takes the robot from engineering builds to production. Our CA facility is where new products are introduced: the process is designed, the first stations are built and proven, and the technicians are trained there. Volume production runs with a manufacturing partner, on their floor or on ours with their people, and you own the process in both cases. You design how the robot gets built, you lead the engineers and technicians who prove it, and you own the quality gate that decides when a unit leaves.

This is hands-on work. You design the first station, write the first work instruction, and bring the partner's team up to our standard. What exists today: an engineering build process with our design team, a production partner, a bill of materials and a plan. What does not exist yet is the production process, and that is the job.

**What you'll do**
------------------

* Design the production process: layout and cycle time, line balancing, station and fixture design, end-of-line test and calibration, material flow.
* Capacity planning: stations, equipment, people and hours by build phase, from the first units to rate, and the plan to add capacity ahead of demand.
* Specify, source and commission fixtures, tooling and test equipment: requirements, RFQ with Supply Chain, acceptance at the vendor and on the floor.
* Own process documentation under revision control: work instructions with photos and video, PFMEA, control plans, inspection plans, SOPs; keep the manufacturing BOM aligned with the engineering BOM and run engineering changes through to the floor.
* Run the transfer from engineering builds to production: pilot builds, DFM and DFA feedback with the authority to push back, build readiness reviews at each phase gate, release to volume.
* Package the process so it can be copied: one documented set of stations, fixtures, test, instructions and training that a partner's floor can run to the same yield as ours.
* Build and lead the team: manufacturing engineers, test engineers and technicians; hiring pace, training and certification, trainer capacity, shift structure as volume grows.
* Own the quality gate: first-pass yield, defect capture, root cause (8D, SPC, DOE where it earns its keep), closed-loop feedback to engineering and suppliers; nothing ships that quality has not passed.
* Partner with Supply Chain on clear-to-build so no unit starts without a complete kit, and with the manufacturing partner so their team runs our process to our standard.
* Stand up the systems as we grow: traceability by serial, MES-lite at first, then the real thing; the weekly numbers (yield, hours per unit, cost per unit, downtime, schedule adherence) and the readout to leadership.

**What we're looking for**
--------------------------

* You have taken a complex electromechanical product from prototype through pilot to volume and designed the process yourself, not inherited it. Robots, vehicles, drones, medical devices, industrial equipment all count.
* You have transferred a process to a contract manufacturer and held them to your standard.
* Strong manufacturing engineering foundation: time studies, line balancing, capacity planning, fixture and tooling design, test strategy, PFMEA and control plans, lean and continuous improvement; CAD and GD&T fluency.
* You have hired and trained technicians, written certification criteria, and know that trained people are the real constraint on throughput.
* You have run a quality gate and held it under schedule pressure.
* You are on the floor every day and rigorous in the data.
* 8 or more years in manufacturing engineering or production, with time in a mature organization so you know what good looks like at scale, and 3 or more years leading people.
* Bonus: actuators, gearboxes or precision assemblies; PLM, MES and ERP implementation; product safety certification processes.

**Working conditions**
----------------------

Production and lab environments; travel to partner sites, up to 25%.

**Why this role**
-----------------

You build the way our robots get built, from the first station to rate, and the process and the team that do it are yours.

**How we work**
---------------

We are always looking for people who are driven to work on hard problems and want to shape what the world will look like in ten years. A few of the values that guide us:

* **Limitless ambition.** We hold ourselves to the highest bar in everything we build.
* **Relentless urgency.** Iterate faster, learn faster. Time is the denominator.
* **Type-2 Fun.** Take the work seriously, not yourself. Embrace the grind and find joy in the struggle.
* **Radical transparency.** Candid communication builds trust, and direct feedback drives growth.
* **Multiculturalism.** We come from across the world. Be curious. Meet people on their terms.
* **Team over ego.** Help others, share context, and win as a team.
* **A joyful journey.** We take pride in the craft.

existing_roles.description:
**Department:** Operations **Job Status:** Full Time

**FLSA Status:** Exempt **Reports To:** President

**Job Type:** Non-Union **Amount of Travel Required:** Occasional

**Work Schedule:** Monday – Friday

Evenings, weekends, Holidays as needed. **Positions Supervised:** Production Staff

**POSITION SUMMARY**

The Director of Manufacturing executes the company operating plan within capital and operating budget parameters. The Director of Manufacturing works with the executive leadership team to develop strategies and objectives to maximize productivity and profitability. Analyzes production trends, forecasts future requirements, solve problems, motivates & develops employees.

**ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS**

**Essential Functions Statement(s)**

 

* Improve operational efficiencies to reduce total production costs while meeting specific product volume needs
* Check and verify production records, handle questions or concerns of inventory shortages or overages and address problems with inventory control.
* Coordinate production schedules to meet sales demand. Adjust production as necessary to meet seasonal demands ahead of schedule.
* Ensure consistency in collective bargaining agreement and provide support during contract negotiations
* Effect necessary communication and motivation to staff. Monitors individual performance via observation and review of various productivity measures. Counsels and disciplines as necessary.
* Provides production required safety leadership and training and is responsible for improved safety performance
* Oversees all production planning and executing against demand signals.
* Oversees facility maintenance team, including Cap-Ex planning and execution.
* Provides input on new product development.
* Ensure compliance with all appropriate health and food safety regulations and cleanliness, including audit preparation
* Manage customer complaint process.
* OSHA, Federal and State requirements are followed with the facility and equipment.
* Attends the Executive, Senior Management, and Safety Committee Meetings
* Maintain work area in a neat, orderly and sanitary manner.
* Correctly and promptly follow specified company procedures required for the appropriate handling of all.
* Emergency Responses and Safety practices.

**POSITION QUALIFICATIONS**

**Competency Statement(s)**

* Communication, Written – Ability to communicate in writing clearly and concisely.
* Collaboration - Collaborates positively to effectively build relationships with customers and co-workers to achieve company objectives and contribute to overall organizational success. Works effectively within a diverse environment. Exhibits a positive attitude and contributes to overall team success.
* Organized – Being organized or following a systematic method of performing a task.
* Communication, Oral – Ability to communicate effectively with others using the spoken word.
* Responsible – Ability to be held accountable or answerable for one’s conduct.
* Honesty / Integrity – Ability to be truthful and be seen as credible in the workplace.
* Accountability – Ability to accept responsibility and account for his/her actions.
* Reliability – The trait of being dependable and trustworthy.

* Customer Oriented – Ability to take care of the customer’s needs while following company procedures.

**Mental Demands:**

* Ability to work under stressful conditions
* Able to interact with others with courtesy and tact
* Ability to manage and prioritize multiple projects in an organized and efficient manner
* Ability to respond to crisis situations in a calm and effective manner

The position requires talking to co-workers, customers, vendors; requires written communications to and from co-workers, customers and vendors, talking on the telephone; requires responding to written or verbal requests of co-workers, customers and vendors; requires training/giving verbal and written instructions; requires receiving verbal and written instructions; requires writing/composing written language; requires reading; requires visiting/working at other work-sites; Ability to communicate via the latest technologies required for the position.

existing_roles.description:
**Company Overview:**

Prime Medicine is a leading biotechnology company dedicated to creating and delivering the next generation of gene editing therapies to patients. The Company is leveraging its proprietary Prime Editing platform, a versatile, precise and efficient gene editing technology, to develop a new class of differentiated, one-time, potentially curative genetic therapies. Designed to make only the right edit at the right position within a gene while minimizing unwanted DNA modifications, Prime Editors have the potential to repair almost all types of genetic mutations and work in many different tissues, organs and cell types.

Prime Medicine is currently progressing a diversified portfolio of investigational therapeutic programs organized around our core areas of focus: hematology, immunology & oncology, liver and lung. Across each core area, Prime Medicine is focused initially on a set of high value programs, each targeting a disease with well-understood biology and a clearly defined clinical development and regulatory path, and each expected to provide the foundation for expansion into additional opportunities. For more information, please visit www.primemedicine.com.

Prime Medicine is a clinical-stage biotechnology company creating the next generation of gene editing therapies. Our Prime Editing platform is versatile, precise, and efficient, with the potential to address more than 90% of known disease-causing genetic mutations. We have three programs in the clinic: an ex vivo cell therapy for an ultra-rare disease advancing toward a Biologics License Application (BLA), and two in vivo liver-targeting LNP Prime Editor programs, with more in development. We are a mission-driven team working in a lean, fast-moving environment.

**Position Overview**
=====================

Reporting directly to the Chief Technology Officer, the Executive Director of Supply Chain and External Manufacturing is a member of the Technology, Development and Operations (TDO) leadership team. You will own Prime Medicine’s end-to-end supply chain, from raw materials through clinical supply and commercialization, with direct accountability for materials management and for supporting internal planning and manufacturing needs. You will manage our external manufacturing partners, lead a highly functional lean team, and serve as the primary partner to Finance for TDO external spend. We are looking for a leader who embraces AI as a core part of how supply chain and external manufacturing run at Prime Medicine, from forecasting and materials visibility to partner performance and cost modeling. This role is for someone who thrives in ambiguity, is energized by building, and pairs strategic thinking with hands-on execution.

**Primary Responsibilities**
============================

* Partner with the CTO and TDO leadership to define manufacturing and supply chain strategy, including network design, make-vs-buy decisions, and partner selection.
* **AI-enabled operations.** Lead the use of AI and digital tools across supply chain and external manufacturing, including demand forecasting, materials and inventory visibility, partner performance monitoring, contract and cost modeling, and logistics tracking, as well as keeping the function ahead of new tools as they emerge.
* **Materials management.** Own materials management across the portfolio, including forecasting, sourcing, purchasing, and inventory of raw materials, critical starting materials, and components, so materials are available on time for each program.
* **Planning and supply operations.** Support internal planning and the manufacturing needs of each program; deliver labeling, packaging, shipping, and cell therapy logistics on time and in full; and resolve supply risks before they affect timelines.
* **External manufacturing and partners.** Build and manage a network of CDMOs, CROs, and critical suppliers, including contracts, governance, performance, and qualification of new partners.
* **Clinical and commercial readiness.** Ensure supply chain documentation and external site readiness support IND and BLA submissions, working with CMC, Regulatory, Quality, Non-clinical Development, Clinical, and program teams.
* Own TDO budget development for external spend, cost projections, and financial reporting in close partnership with functional leaders and Finance.
* **Leadership**. Lead, coach, and inspire your team of supply chain/external manufacturing professionals and indirect colleagues across TDO; foster a culture of accountability, continuous improvement, and collaborative problem-solving and goal attainment

**Preferred Qualifications**
============================

* Bachelor’s degree in a relevant technical discipline; advanced degree (MS, MBA, or PhD) preferred
* 15–20+ years of progressive experience in supply chain, technical operations, external manufacturing, process development, or MSAT within biotech or pharma
* Direct ownership of materials management and clinical supply for clinical-stage programs
* Experience managing CDMOs and CROs, including negotiating MSAs and SOWs
* Experience with cell therapy and/or LNP or nucleic acid programs; experience supporting IND/CTA and BLA/MAA submissions
* Financial acumen, including ownership of operating budgets and multi-year cost projections
* Track record of implementing AI or digital tools that improved forecasting, visibility, or decision-making in supply chain or operations, and of changing how teams work as a result
* Strong change management, project management, and communication skills, with the ability to build trust with partners, Finance, and senior leadership
* Plus: lean, fast-moving biotech; ultra-rare disease or small patient population experience

**Why Prime Medicine**
======================

Your work will matter: our programs have the potential to be curative therapies for patients with no other options, and this role directly enables that. You will be part of the TDO leadership team, with direct access to the CTO and interact with other Executive leaders, and you will shape how AI is applied to supply chain and manufacturing at a company where it is a growing priority. You will have ownership from day one in building how Prime Medicine delivers for patients.

Prime Medicine is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, sexual orientation, gender identity, disability, veteran status, or any other classification protected by law.

Location: Cambridge, MA | Reports to: Chief Technology Officer | TDO Leadership Team Member

The pay range reflects the full-time base salary range we expect to pay for this role at the time of posting. Base pay will be determined based on several factors including, but not limited to, relevant experience, skills, and education. This role is eligible for an annual short-term incentive award (e.g., bonus) and an annual long-term incentive award (e.g., equity).

Prime Medicine offers a comprehensive Total Rewards package with robust health, financial, and wellness benefits—including medical, dental, vision, life insurance, a 401(k) match, and equity programs—along with generous paid time off, wellness days, and company-wide recharge breaks.

Our commitment to employee well-being reflects our belief that when we care for our people, we strengthen our ability to put patients first and make meaningful impact together.

$295,000 - $312,000 USD

existing_roles.description:
Formica is a name people know. Our laminate was introduced in Cincinnati more than a century ago, and our products are found in homes and businesses around the world. Today we are a global leader in building products and surface materials, and part of Broadview Holding alongside sister companies Trespa, Arpa, and Westag.

Our 1-million-square-foot Evendale site is in the middle of a transformation, and we are looking for a **Director of Manufacturing** to lead it. This is not a role for someone who wants to maintain the status quo. It is for an action-driven leader who wants to roll up their sleeves, raise the bar, and build a plant that performs at a best-in-class level and stays there.

**About the Role**

Reporting to the Vice President of Operations, the Director of Manufacturing leads day-to-day operations at Evendale, with direct accountability for health, safety and environment; quality; production; maintenance; engineering; production planning; and warehousing. You will be a key member of the Operations leadership team and the person who sets the pace for change on the floor.

**What You’ll Do**

* Lead the site’s transformation: develop and carry out the strategy and operating plan that moves Evendale to best-in-class performance
* Bring urgency and energy to the floor, and build a culture of accountability, ownership, and follow-through at every level
* Drive safety, quality, and performance to clear targets, including zero recordable injuries, 98% first-pass yield, OEE above 80%, and OTIF above 96%
* Lead Lean and continuous improvement, including 5S, visual management, Gemba walks, Kaizen, 80/20, and Six Sigma
* Build a clear maintenance strategy that keeps improving equipment reliability
* Own the annual budget, including capital projects and improvement savings
* Coach and develop leaders, and build succession plans for critical roles

**What You Bring**

* 10–15 years of progressive experience leading operations in a medium- to large-sized manufacturing organization
* A demonstrated track record of change leadership: you have lifted a site or operation, identified challenges, changed the culture, and made the results last
* Hands-on leadership across safety, quality, maintenance, and production
* Deep, practical experience with Lean manufacturing and continuous improvement
* A history of staying, building, and seeing the work through
* Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, or in Business with an Operations Management focus

**Strongly preferred:** experience leading an organized labor workforce, including union contract negotiations, and a background in process manufacturing or building products.

**How You Lead**

* **Transformation leader:** You have led real change and are energized by closing the gap between where things are and where they need to be.
* **Action driver:** You turn plans into action, follow through, and expect the same from your team.
* **Direct and assertive:** You bring a clear point of view and hold it, while listening to others.
* **Constructive negotiator:** You find common ground and reach agreements without creating conflict.
* **Developer of people:** You have grown successors and build leaders who bring the same energy.

**Why Formica**

Ask people at Formica why they work here and many will tell you the answer is simple: they love the brand, the company, and the products. We are a collaborative community of independent thinkers, and we back our people with real tools for growing their careers.

We offer a competitive package, including base salary and an annual incentive opportunity, plus medical, dental, and vision coverage; a 401(k) with a company match of up to 4%, immediately vested; 15 days of PTO from your start date plus 11 paid holidays; and company-paid short-term disability and life insurance.

Candidates in Ohio and the Cincinnati region are preferred. Strong candidates from other areas are welcome.

#### **Education**

Preferred

* Bachelors or better

existing_roles.description:
**Company Description**

**About AbbVie**

AbbVie's mission is to discover and deliver innovative medicines and solutions that solve serious health issues today and address the medical challenges of tomorrow. We strive to have a remarkable impact on people's lives across several key therapeutic areas including immunology, oncology and neuroscience - and products and services in our Allergan Aesthetics portfolio. For more information about AbbVie, please visit us at www.abbvie.com. Follow @abbvie on LinkedIn, Facebook, Instagram, X and YouTube.

 **Job Description**

**New to North Carolina. Known for pursuing breakthroughs in medicine.**

**Ready to join our team?**

At AbbVie, we bring together talented people and innovative science to develop medicines that help patients. Now, we’re bringing that commitment to Durham, North Carolina, with a new manufacturing campus that will expand our ability to produce medicines and create opportunities in the Research Triangle.

The campus will integrate advanced manufacturing, laboratory technologies and AI to support the production of immunology, oncology and neuroscience medicines. The first phase will include manufacturing facilities, next-generation laboratories, a warehouse, administrative offices and employee wellness facilities.

We are now recruiting our **Project Director / Manufacturing Director, Operations as part of the core start up leadership team.**

In this role, you will provide leadership and direction for a manufacturing operation of a large site (drug substance, drug product, biologics and/or aseptic sterile fill finish) delivering multiple products, technically complex products, and in support of new product introductions, readiness for launch.

**Key Responsibilities**

 

* Partnering with the leadership team, help build and establish the site - from recruiting the key talent needed for your team to establishing operational readiness
* Create operational and financial goals, budgets and objectives for the assigned manufacturing area. Manage budget of typically $60MM or more, ensure performance levels to maximize operations.
* Apply a high level of scientific analysis and decision-making to influence the design and ongoing optimization of manufacturing processes. Provide leadership to teams when troubleshooting manufacturing issues; consults and advises cross-functional teams to ensure processes and approaches result in efficient, high quality products.
* Drive and lead the assigned manufacturing area to meet the site business strategies; accountable for operating expenses, payroll and capital expenditures for manufacturing area projects and programs.
* Guide development and implementation of business strategies to achieve budget expectations as well as drive cost reduction efforts; implement actions to adapt and transform the organization in order to meet changing business needs.
* Ensure staff members are provided training and coaching to build technical knowledge and capability.
* Responsible for synthesizing action plans, timelines and budgets for project and product goals and adjusting these plans accordingly to effectively respond to changing demands of the business.
* Develop and manage staff through hiring, managing performance, developing talent and providing clear expectations.
* Ensure all labor and equipment performance measures are met. Responsible for completing established goals, prioritizing project work and controlling and coordinating all activities and improvement efforts across manufacturing areas.
* Manage the employee relations climate to ensure that our AbbVie Way is realized and an environment exists where all employees have the opportunity to develop to their maximum potential.
* Coach managers in the organization and establish clear expectations with them and all employees regarding responsibilities, goals and behaviors and champion and model exceptional AbbVie performance and talent management practices.

 
**Qualifications** 

* Bachelor’s Degree required in a related technical field such as Chemical Engineering: advanced technical degree (Master’s or Doctorate Degree) strongly preferred
* 12+ years’ experience including: work as an individual contributor building technical expertise and proved project management skills. Progressively increased responsibility and performance as supervisor, department manager and leader of diverse teams in Operations (Manufacturing, Quality, Supply Chain, Engineering, etc.)
* 8+ years expeirence in a simiilar drug substance, drug product, biologics and/or aseptic sterile fill finish environment is required
* You will have demonstrated your ability to lead successful teams in prior roles and experience in partnering cross functionally in a GMP manufacturing environment
* Business acumen coupled with functional leadership experience is required to ensure effectiveness and high performance in a complex operation
* Travel up to 50% during the initial start up phase of the project

.

Applicable only to applicants applying to a position in any location with pay disclosure requirements under state or local law:

* The compensation range described below is the range of possible base pay compensation that the Company believes in good faith it will pay for this role at the time of this posting based on the job grade for this position. Individual compensation paid within this range will depend on many factors including geographic location, and we may ultimately pay more or less than the posted range. This range may be modified in the future.
* We offer a comprehensive package of benefits including paid time off (vacation, holidays, sick), medical/dental/vision insurance and 401(k) to eligible employees.
* This job is eligible to participate in our long-term incentive programs.

Note: No amount of pay is considered to be wages or compensation until such amount is earned, vested, and determinable. The amount and availability of any bonus, commission, incentive, benefits, or any other form of compensation and benefits that are allocable to a particular employee remains in the Company's sole and absolute discretion unless and until paid and may be modified at the Company’s sole and absolute discretion, consistent with applicable law.

Office

**Job Description**

As part of the Thermo Fisher Scientific team, you’ll discover meaningful work that makes a positive impact on a global scale. Join our colleagues in bringing our Mission to life every single day to enable our customers to make the world healthier, cleaner and safer. We provide our global teams with the resources needed to achieve individual career goals while helping to take science a step beyond by developing solutions for some of the world’s toughest challenges, like protecting the environment, making sure our food is safe or helping find cures for cancer. 
 
DESCRIPTION: 
Join Thermo Fisher Scientific as a Senior Manager, Plant/Site and contribute to global science and healthcare. You'll oversee operations at advanced facilities, ensuring the delivery of high-quality products that help our customers make the world healthier, cleaner, and safer. This leadership role involves advancing operational excellence through Lean manufacturing principles, managing cross-functional teams, and implementing continuous improvement initiatives. 
 
As the site leader, you'll be responsible for developing and executing strategic plans, ensuring regulatory compliance, and maintaining strong customer relationships. You'll support our core values of Integrity, Intensity, Innovation, and Involvement while cultivating a culture of safety, quality, and operational excellence. This role offers the opportunity to implement positive change, support team development, and contribute to scientific advances. 
 
REQUIREMENTS: 

* Advanced Degree plus 6 years of experience, or Bachelor's Degree plus 8 years of experience in operations leadership in sophisticated manufacturing environments
* Preferred Fields of Study: Engineering, Science, Business Management, or related field
* Strong track record implementing Lean Manufacturing and continuous improvement methodologies
* Experience leading teams in FDA-regulated, cGMP, ISO 13485, or similar quality systems
* Demonstrated financial acumen in budget management and operational cost control
* Excellence in developing and executing strategic and annual operating plans
* Proven ability to build and lead high-performing teams in matrix organizations
* Strong project management skills with ability to manage multiple concurrent initiatives
* Experience with quality systems, regulatory compliance, and audit management
* Expert knowledge of operational KPIs and data-driven process improvement
* Outstanding communication and interpersonal skills across all organizational levels

* Proficiency in leading change management initiatives

* Experience of working in a unionized environment.
* Strong analytical and problem-solving capabilities
* Ability to travel up to 10-15% as required
* Experience maintaining safety programs and environmental compliance
* Excellent vendor and customer relationship management skills

**Compensation and Benefits**

The salary range estimated for this position based in Connecticut is $131,300.00–$205,000.00.

This position may also be eligible to receive a variable annual bonus based on company, team, and/or individual performance results in accordance with company policy. We offer a comprehensive Total Rewards package that our U.S. colleagues and their families can count on, which includes:

* A choice of national medical and dental plans, and a national vision plan, including health incentive programs
* Employee assistance and family support programs, including commuter benefits and tuition reimbursement
* At least 120 hours paid time off (PTO), 10 paid holidays annually, paid parental leave (3 weeks for bonding and 8 weeks for caregiver leave), accident and life insurance, and short- and long-term disability in accordance with company policy
* Retirement and savings programs, such as our competitive 401(k) U.S. retirement savings plan
* Employees’ Stock Purchase Plan (ESPP) offers eligible colleagues the opportunity to purchase company stock at a discount

For more information on our benefits, please visit: https://jobs.thermofisher.com/global/en/total-rewards

Overview:

**WHO WE ARE**

As the largest private-sector power producer in the world and the nation's largest producer of clean and reliable energy, Constellation is focused on our purpose: lighting the way to a brilliant tomorrow for all. We have been the leader in clean energy production for more than a decade, and we are cultivating a workplace where our employees can grow, thrive, and contribute. Now integrated with Calpine, our portfolio includes 55 gigawatts of capacity from nuclear, natural gas, geothermal, hydro, wind and solar facilities, with the generating capacity to power the equivalent of 27 million homes. 
 
Our culture and employee experience make it clear: We are powered by passion and purpose. Together, we're creating healthier communities and a cleaner planet, and our people are the driving force behind our success. At Constellation, you can build a fulfilling career with opportunities to learn, grow and make an impact. By doing our best work and meeting new challenges, we can accomplish great things. Join us in meeting the country's energy needs today and tomorrow.

**TOTAL REWARDS**

Constellation offers an extensive selection of benefits and rewards to help our employees thrive professionally and personally. We provide competitive compensation and a wide-range of benefits that support both employees and their families, helping them prepare for the future. In addition to highly competitive salaries, eligible employees are offered a bonus program, 401(k) with company match, employee stock purchase program; comprehensive medical, dental and vision benefits, including robust wellbeing programs; disability and life insurance benefits; paid time off for vacation, holidays, and sick days; and much more.

Expected salary range of $189,000 to $210,000, varies based on experience, along with comprehensive benefits package that includes bonus and 401(k).

Responsibilities:

**PRIMARY PURPOSE OF POSITION**

Manage and oversee the safe, efficient and reliable operation of fossil or hydro station(s). Ensure compliance with all federal, state and local regulatory requirements, applicable industry technical standards and company policies. Operate the plant(s) in a manner that minimizes the cost of generation and maximizes profitability while maintaining the long-term viability of the station assets.

**PRIMARY DUTIES AND ACCOUNTABILITIES**

 

* Ensure standards are established and implemented to provide a safe work environment.
* Effectively manage all resources to ensure generation of electricity in a timely and reliable manner at the direction of the Power Team.
* Maintain a positive work environment and good employee relations. Provide guidance for employee development opportunities and timely feedback regarding performance.
* Serve as a change agent for business initiatives, while assuring the human element is understood and considered
* Manage the station O&M and capital budgets to minimize costs and maximize profitability while ensuring the long-term viability of the assets.
* Ensure compliance with all federal, state and local regulatory requirements and maintain environmental stewardship.
* Maintain effective community relations to promote a positive image of the Company.
* Perform all other duties as assigned.

**MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS**

 

* BS in engineering or business
* Minimum of 10 years professional experience
* Minimum of 8 years power plant (or related) experience
* Minimum of 5 years supervisory/managerial experience
* Professional or technical level experience in a technical role at a power plant
* Operations
* At least 2 of the following: Corporate/Staff, Engineering, Maintenance, or Outage
* Leadership assessment required

 
Qualifications:

**PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS**

 

* Master's Degree in engineering, business or related field
* Multi-site experience
* Multi-departmental experience
* Collective bargaining experience

existing_roles.description:
Overview:

**Who We Are**

As the largest private-sector power producer in the world and the nation's largest producer of clean and reliable energy, Constellation is focused on our purpose: lighting the way to a brilliant tomorrow for all. We have been the leader in clean energy production for more than a decade, and we are cultivating a workplace where our employees can grow, thrive, and contribute. Now integrated with Calpine, our portfolio includes 55 gigawatts of capacity from nuclear, natural gas, geothermal, hydro, wind and solar facilities, with the generating capacity to power the equivalent of 27 million homes. 
 
Our culture and employee experience make it clear: We are powered by passion and purpose. Together, we're creating healthier communities and a cleaner planet, and our people are the driving force behind our success. At Constellation, you can build a fulfilling career with opportunities to learn, grow and make an impact. By doing our best work and meeting new challenges, we can accomplish great things. Join us in meeting the country's energy needs today and tomorrow.

**Total Rewards**

Constellation offers an extensive selection of benefits and rewards to help our employees thrive professionally and personally. We provide competitive compensation and a wide-range of benefits that support both employees and their families, helping them prepare for the future. In addition to highly competitive salaries, eligible employees are offered a bonus program, 401(k) with company match, employee stock purchase program; comprehensive medical, dental and vision benefits, including robust wellbeing programs; disability and life insurance benefits; paid time off for vacation, holidays, and sick days; and much more.

Expected salary range of $211,500 to $235,000, varies based on experience, along with comprehensive benefits package that includes bonus and 401(k).

Responsibilities:

**Primary Purpose of Position**

Overall accountability for equipment reliability to ensure operating requirements meet quality standards at the lowest possible cost. Manage and oversee the safe, efficient and reliable operation of fossil and/or hydro station(s) in the Exelon Power fleet. Ensure compliance with all federal, state and local regulatory requirements, applicable industry technical standards and company policies. Operate the plant(s) in a manner that minimizes the cost of generation and maximizes profitability while maintaining the long-term viability of the station assets.

**Primary Duties and Accountabilities**

 

* Manage all resources to ensure generation of electricity in a timely and reliable manner at the direction of the Power Team.
* Create and manage the station O&M and capital budgets to minimize the costs and maximize profitability while ensuring the long-term viability of the assets.
* Maintain a positive work environment and good employee relations. Provide guidance for employee development opportunities and timely feedback regarding performance. Serve as a change agent for business initiatives. Assure proper administration of collective bargaining agreement, if applicable, and company programs and policies, including safety, attendance, discipline, etc.
* Ensure Power standards and fundamentals are established and implemented to provide a safe work environment.
* Ensure compliance with all federal, state and local regulatory requirements and maintain environmental stewardship.
* Maintain effective community relations to promote a positive image of the Company.
* Participate in ESG- and GHG-related meetings, conferences, and workshops to enhance professional knowledge and stay abreast of industry trends.

**Minimum Qualifications**

 

* Bachelor's Degree in Business or a Technical Program and 12 years of experience
* 15-years professional experience
* 10-years of power plant (or related) experience
* 5-years supervisor/management experience
* Collective bargaining experience
* Experience in 2 of the following: Operations, Engineering, Maintenance, or Outage
* Plant operations and maintenance experience
* Leadership assessment required
* Strong communication and interpersonal skills
* Strong problem-solving, conflict resolution, organizational and analytical skills
* Flexibility to handle multiple daily deadlines and adapt to changing priorities

 
Qualifications:

**Preferred Qualifications**

 

* Master's degree in business or related field
* Multi-site experience
* Multi-departmental experience

existing_roles.description:
**Work Location: Newington, CT. This is an in person role, not remote, not hybrid**
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------

**Work Schedule: Monday - Friday; 8:30 am - 5:00 pm**

**SUMMARY**
-----------

The Plant Manager is responsible for the overall leadership, management, and performance of the Data-Graphics manufacturing facility. This position directs all aspects of plant operations, including production, quality, safety, maintenance, staffing, and continuous improvement initiatives. The Plant Manager ensures production commitments are met while maintaining high quality standards, maximizing operational efficiency, controlling costs, and fostering a culture of accountability, teamwork, and safety.

The Plant Manager provides strategic and hands-on leadership to achieve key performance indicators (KPIs), customer satisfaction goals, employee engagement objectives, and business growth initiatives.

**ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES**
=========================================

**Operations Management**

* Direct and oversee all day-to-day plant operations, including production, scheduling, quality, safety, maintenance and receiving activities.
* Ensure production schedules are met while maintaining quality standards, delivery commitments, and operational efficiency.
* Develop, monitor, and achieve plant performance metrics related to productivity, quality, waste reduction, safety, downtime, labor utilization, and customer satisfaction.
* Collaborate with sales, customer service, prepress, and production teams to ensure customer expectations are consistently met or exceeded.
* Establish priorities and allocate resources to support production requirements and business objectives.
* Analyze operational performance and implement corrective actions as needed to improve productivity and profitability.

**Leadership & Employee Development**

* Lead, coach, and develop supervisors, and production personnel to maximize performance and engagement.
* Promote a culture of accountability, continuous improvement, teamwork, professionalism, and employee development.
* Conduct performance evaluations, establish performance expectations, and provide ongoing coaching and feedback.
* Partner with Human Resources on workforce planning, employee relations matters, recruitment, retention, performance management, and disciplinary actions.
* Ensure employees receive appropriate training and development opportunities to support operational excellence.

**Quality Management**

* Champion quality initiatives to ensure products consistently meet customer specifications and company quality standards.
* Investigate quality concerns and implement corrective and preventive actions to eliminate recurring issues.
* Monitor production processes and identify opportunities for process improvement and defect reduction.
* Work closely with client services and suppliers to address quality-related concerns and maintain strong business relationships.

**Safety & Regulatory Compliance**

* Ensure compliance with all company safety policies, environmental regulations, and applicable OSHA requirements.
* Promote and maintain a safe work environment through training, audits, inspections, and corrective actions.
* Conduct regular safety reviews and support accident investigation and root cause analysis activities.
* Ensure appropriate personal protective equipment (PPE) is utilized and safety procedures are consistently followed.

**Maintenance & Continuous Improvement**

* Oversee preventive maintenance programs to maximize equipment reliability and minimize downtime.
* Drive Lean Manufacturing, continuous improvement, waste reduction, and cost-saving initiatives throughout the facility.
* Evaluate equipment, processes, and workflows to identify opportunities for increased efficiency and operational effectiveness.
* Develop and implement strategies to improve throughput, reduce spoilage, and optimize labor utilization.

**Financial Management**

* Develop and manage departmental budgets and operational expenses.
* Monitor labor costs, production costs, and capital expenditures to ensure financial targets are achieved.
* Participate in forecasting, strategic planning, and capital investment decisions affecting the facility.

**Communication & Reporting**

* Communicate operational results, goals, and key initiatives to leadership and employees.
* Prepare and present reports on plant performance, production metrics, quality trends, safety performance, and continuous improvement initiatives.
* Keep executive management informed of significant operational issues, risks, and opportunities.
* Perform other duties as assigned in support of company objectives.

**EDUCATION / EXPERIENCE**

* Bachelor's degree in Business Administration, Operations Management, Engineering, Manufacturing, or a related field preferred.
* Minimum of 7-10 years of progressive manufacturing leadership experience.
* Minimum of 5 years of management experience overseeing production operations and employees.
* Printing, packaging, direct mail, graphic communications, or related manufacturing industry experience strongly preferred.
* Demonstrated experience leading continuous improvement initiatives and operational excellence programs.
* Experience managing budgets, KPIs, production planning, and quality systems.

**COMPETENCIES**

**Leadership**

* Strong leadership and team-building abilities
* Ability to motivate and develop employees at all levels
* Effective coaching, mentoring, and performance management skills
* Strong decision-making and problem-solving abilities

**Operational Excellence**

* Knowledge of manufacturing operations and process improvement methodologies
* Understanding of Lean Manufacturing and continuous improvement principles
* Experience utilizing production metrics and KPIs to drive results
* Strong project management and organizational skills

**Technical Knowledge**

* Knowledge of printing operations, lithographic printing, flexographic printing, finishing, and mailing operations preferred
* Understanding of quality management systems and root cause analysis techniques
* Knowledge of maintenance planning and equipment reliability principles

**Communication & Business Skills**

* Excellent written, verbal, and interpersonal communication skills
* Strong analytical and financial acumen
* Proficiency with Microsoft Office, including Excel, Word, and Outlook
* Ability to effectively manage customer, vendor, and employee relationships

**Job Description:**

**Job Title:**

**Senior Plant Manager** (Corona, CA)

**Collaborate with Innovative 3Mers Around the World**

Choosing where to start and grow your career has a major impact on your professional and personal life, so it’s equally important you know that the company that you choose to work at, and its leaders, will support and guide you. With a wide variety of people, global locations, technologies and products, 3M is a place where you can collaborate with 96,000 other curious, creative 3Mers.

**This position provides an opportunity to transition from other private, public, government or military environments to a 3M career.**

**The Impact You’ll Make in this Role** 
As the **Senior Plant Manager,** you will have the opportunity to tap into your curiosity and collaborate with some of the most innovative people around the world. Here, you will make an impact by:

 

* Active and visible EHS ownership to ensure site compliance, stewardship and championing continuous improvement efforts to improve all aspects of EHS.
* Accountable for strategic planning and budgeting to drive sustainable improvements in factory cost through application of Lean Six Sigma, entitlement thinking, yield improvement, plant productivity and capital planning.
* Implement lean manufacturing principles and methodology to drive employee engagement and continuous improvement, with a strong focus on TPM, 5S and Standard work.
* Managing supply chain execution and inventory management to ensure appropriate supply chain performance through responsiveness, delivery performance, capacity management, supplier management, and appropriate inventory management.
* Represent 3M and engage with key accounts.
* Engaging the community by representing 3M in community affairs as appropriate and foster good public relations in the local community.

**Your Skills and Expertise**

To set you up for success in this role from day one, 3M requires (at a minimum) the following qualifications:

 

* Bachelor's degree or higher (completed and verified prior to start)
* Three (3) years of supervisory and/or management experience in a private, public, government or military environment
* Five (5) years of manufacturing experience in a private, public, government or military environment

Additional qualifications that could help you succeed even further in this role include:

 

* Certified LSS BB or MBB
* Experience in Operations Management
* Union experience a plus
* Expert knowledge and experience in production management, lean manufacturing and materials control
* Strong Communication and Change Management skills
* Experience in Lean manufacturing methodologies in driving value stream improvement.
* Prior Plant Manager Experience

existing_roles.description:
Founded in 1967, ImageFIRST® is the largest and only national linen rental and laundry service specializing in the healthcare market. Acquired by private equity firm Calera Capital in 2018, ImageFIRST serves medical facilities nationwide providing linen, patient gowns, scrubs, and more while managing their clients’ linen inventory for cost management. As leaders in infection prevention, they currently own and operate the most HLAC-accredited facilities in the industry. With one of the highest customer retention rates in the industry – 97% – ImageFIRST is dedicated to improving patient satisfaction and making staff happy with our white glove service!

Check out our company page: https://www.imagefirst.com/company/

**Director, Operational Excellence - CAPEX**
============================================

**Location:** East Coast (Northeast Preferred) 
**Travel:** Approximately 50%

**Position Summary**
--------------------

ImageFIRST is seeking a strategic, hands-on **Director, Operational Excellence** to lead enterprise-wide engineering initiatives, capital project planning, and operational improvement efforts across our national network of healthcare laundry facilities.

This newly created leadership role will serve as a key partner to Operations and the Senior Leadership Team, driving long-term asset strategy, **capital investment planning**, engineering support, and operational sustainability. The ideal candidate is equally comfortable developing strategic initiatives, leading complex projects, and rolling up their sleeves to solve operational challenges in the field.

This role offers a unique opportunity to build foundational processes that will standardize engineering practices and strengthen operational performance across the organization.

**Key Responsibilities**
------------------------

### **Capital Planning & Strategic Investments**

* Identify, prioritize, and develop capital expenditure (Capex) opportunities across the network.
* Build financial justifications, ROI analyses, and business cases for capital investments.
* Present capital recommendations and project proposals to the Senior Leadership Team.
* Partner with Finance and Operations to align capital investments with business strategy and growth objectives.

### **Project Engineering Leadership**

* Lead enterprise engineering projects from concept through implementation.
* Provide technical leadership for facility upgrades, equipment installations, automation initiatives, and operational improvements.
* Ensure projects are completed safely, on schedule, within budget, and with measurable business impact.

### **Engineering Support for Plant Operations**

* Serve as a technical resource for manufacturing and plant leadership across the ImageFIRST network.
* Provide engineering guidance and problem-solving support for facilities requiring operational or technical assistance.
* Partner with General Managers and Operations Leaders to resolve complex equipment and process challenges.

### **Operational Excellence & Strategic Initiatives**

* Lead cross-functional operational improvement initiatives that support network stabilization, sustainability, and long-term operational performance.
* Partner with Operations Leadership to identify opportunities for increased efficiency, standardization, and continuous improvement.
* Serve as a trusted resource for high-impact operational projects across the business.

### **Safety Leadership**

* Champion a culture of safety across engineering and operational initiatives.
* Ensure engineering projects and equipment installations meet all applicable safety standards and regulatory requirements.
* Partner with Environmental Health & Safety leadership to proactively reduce operational risk.

**Qualifications**
------------------

### **Required**

* Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Operations Management, Industrial Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, or a related discipline (or equivalent combination of education and experience).
* 10+ years of progressive leadership experience in manufacturing, industrial operations, engineering, or capital project management.
* Experience leading multi-site engineering or operational initiatives.
* Proven experience managing capital projects and developing ROI-driven business cases.
* Strong knowledge of asset management, equipment lifecycle planning, and reliability.
* Demonstrated ability to lead cross-functional teams and influence stakeholders at all organizational levels.
* Strong financial acumen with experience presenting recommendations to executive leadership.
* Ability to travel approximately 50%.

### **Preferred**

* Experience supporting multiple manufacturing or industrial facilities.
* Plant management or operations leadership experience.
* Lean Manufacturing, TPM, Six Sigma, or Continuous Improvement experience.
* Military leadership experience is highly valued, particularly candidates who have transitioned into manufacturing, engineering, or operations leadership roles.
* Experience within healthcare services, industrial laundry, textiles, food manufacturing, consumer products, or other asset-intensive industries.

**Leadership Competencies**
---------------------------

* Strategic thinker with strong operational execution
* Results-oriented and highly accountable
* Excellent communication and executive presentation skills
* Strong analytical and financial decision-making capabilities
* Collaborative leadership style with the ability to influence across functions
* Comfortable navigating ambiguity and leading enterprise-wide change
* Hands-on problem solver with a continuous improvement mindset

**Required Competencies:**

* Be Respectful: Value all we come in contact with
* Be Remarkable: Create a positive moment with every interaction
* Be Safe: Keep ourselves and those around us safe
* Be Honest: Be guided by truthfulness in all we do

**Benefits:**

* Weekly pay
* Medical, Dental, Vision
* Pet, Legal, and Hospital Indemnity Insurance
* 401k (match)
* Paid Time Off Package
* Paid Parental Leave
* Tuition Reimbursement
* Referral Program

existing_roles.title: Vice President, Quality & Food Safety
existing_roles.description:
Description:

**Who We Are**

Headquartered in Vineland, NJ, F&S Fresh Foods is leading the way in fresh-cut fruit, vegetables, and meal solutions distribution. With the recent acquisition of five additional state-of-the-art facilities strategically located across the U.S., we now deliver to customers across the United States and Canada — every single day!

For over 40 years, we’ve been redefining production and safety processes, building strong partnerships, and creating endless possibilities for our diverse customers — from restaurants and supermarket prepared food operations to convenience store chains and beyond. At F&S, we are fueling families with nutrition, innovation, and convenience, turning meals into memorable moments. By combining cutting-edge technology, deep-rooted customer relationships, and operational excellence, we are shaping the future of fresh — from farm to family.

We’re not just about food; we’re about people. Recognized as a Great Place to Work for three consecutive years, our team of 2,100 full-time employees drives our culture forward by living our values every day. If you’re ready to be part of a company that values innovation, excellence, and community impact, join us as we embrace our next exciting chapter of growth. Together, we’re planting the seeds of progress and nourishing a fresh, healthy future for everyone!

**What We Offer**

* Competitive compensation package
* Comprehensive benefits: Medical, Dental, Vision and Life Insurance
* 401(K) including company match!
* Paid Time Off annually + Paid Holidays
* Career Advancement opportunities and Tuition Assistance

**What’s the Role**

The Vice President, Quality & Food Safety is F&S Fresh Foods’ senior executive leader for Quality Assurance, Food Safety, Regulatory Compliance, Supplier Quality, and Customer Quality across all of our facilities. This role sets the enterprise-wide strategy, standards, and systems that keep our products safe, consistent, and compliant with every regulatory, customer, and certification requirement. As the company’s senior authority on food safety risk, audit readiness, and crisis management, you will protect consumers, customers, and the F&S brand while partnering closely with Operations, Supply Chain, Procurement, Product Development, Sales, and Executive Leadership. The ideal candidate is a strategic, data-driven leader who earns the trust of customers and regulators, develops strong teams, and champions a culture where food safety and quality are everyone’s responsibility.

**What You’ll Own**

* Set and execute the long-term Quality and Food Safety strategy, including enterprise goals, standards, KPIs, and governance processes aligned with business objectives
* Lead all corporate Quality Assurance, Food Safety, Regulatory Compliance, Supplier Quality, and Customer Quality functions, ensuring consistent programs across all facilities
* Own the enterprise Food Safety Management System, including HACCP, Preventive Controls, Environmental Monitoring, Allergen Management, Traceability, Food Defense, and pathogen control
* Establish and maintain enterprise quality management systems so products consistently meet specifications, customer expectations, and regulatory requirements
* Ensure compliance with FDA, USDA, FSMA, GFSI, state, local, and customer requirements, interpreting emerging regulations and maintaining audit and inspection readiness at every site
* Serve as senior liaison with regulatory agencies, certification bodies, and customer auditors, overseeing closure of audit findings, regulatory actions, and corrective actions
* Serve as executive authority and decision-maker for food safety incidents, recalls, and crisis response, maintaining risk assessment, traceability, mock recall, and incident management programs
* Represent F&S during customer visits, audits, business reviews, and quality events, building strategic relationships and leading resolution of significant complaints and brand-risk events
* Partner with Commercial, Product Development, and Operations to support growth while maintaining product integrity and improving customer satisfaction
* Establish supplier approval, audit, and monitoring standards and drive supplier performance improvement, partnering with Procurement to mitigate supply chain risk
* Drive data-based improvement to reduce defects, waste, and customer complaints and improve process capability, publishing executive dashboards and performance updates for leadership
* Lead and develop Directors, Managers, and technical leaders, building succession plans, bench strength, and a culture of accountability, engagement, and high performance
* Establish enterprise training standards and competency requirements, partnering with Operations and Human Resources to build food safety and quality into talent development and performance management
* Champion a companywide culture where food safety and quality are everyone’s responsibility, promoting proactive risk identification and continuous improvement
* Serve as the company’s senior subject matter expert on food safety, quality systems, microbiology, compliance, and regulatory matters
* Participate in strategic planning, acquisition integration activities, and enterprise transformation initiatives

Requirements:

**What You Bring**

* Must have: Bachelor’s degree in Food Science, Microbiology, Food Technology, Engineering, or a related scientific discipline; Master’s degree preferred
* Must have: HACCP and Preventive Controls Qualified Individual (PCQI) certifications
* Must have: 15+ years of progressive Quality and Food Safety leadership, including 7+ years leading multi-site organizations
* Must have: Extensive experience in fresh, refrigerated, ready-to-eat, produce, protein, or other highly regulated food manufacturing
* Must have: Proven success leading customer audits, regulatory inspections, certification audits, recalls, and crisis events
* Must have: Strong knowledge of FDA, USDA, FSMA, GFSI, Environmental Monitoring Programs, and Quality Systems
* Nice to have: Lead Auditor, SQF Practitioner, BRCGS, or equivalent certification
* Personal quality: Strategic, consumer- and customer-focused decision-maker who uses metrics, risk assessments, and audit results to set priorities while balancing operational and commercial objectives
* Personal quality: Executive presence and influence with customers, regulators, and leadership, with a track record of building high-performing teams and delivering measurable results

Notice Regarding the Use of Artificial Intelligence in Application Review

**Notice of AI Use in Job Application Review**

As part of our commitment in creating a fair, efficient, and consistent hiring process we may use artificial intelligence (AI) to help our recruiting teams organize, summarize, and analyze information provided by candidates, including resumes, application responses, and other materials submitted during the application process.AI may be used to identify patterns, highlight relevant skills, and experience, and assist in comparing a candidate’s qualifications with the requirement of a specific role. These tools are to improve efficiency and consistency while supporting more informed hiring decisions, which will ultimately be made by the hiring team.
